items.stem: Which function returns the whole number of complete years between a hire date and today?

options.rationale: Correct: DATEDIF(start, end, "Y") returns complete years.
TODAY returns the current date, not an interval.
Adding dates does not yield an interval in years.
TEXT formats a value; it does not compute an interval.

items.explanation: Correct: DATEDIF(start, end, "Y") returns the number of complete years.

items.stem: Why should payroll deduction rates live in a separate rate table rather than inside each formula?

options.text: So a rate change is made once and flows through every calculation
options.rationale: Correct: centralising rates makes updates safe and auditable.

options.text: Because Excel cannot multiply without a table
options.rationale: Excel multiplies values directly; this is a design choice.
A rate table does not meaningfully change file size.

options.text: Because formulas cannot reference other cells

items.explanation: Correct: a central rate table means a change is made once and flows through every formula.
